PARIS — France will develop a next-generation combat aircraft domestically as a successor to the Rafale, after a joint project with Germany and Spain for a future combat air system collapsed earlier this year, Air and Space Force Chief of Staff Jérôme Bellanger said.
The country now conceives the future fighter, dubbed Avion de Combat du Futur or ACF, as a national project, with a target of flying conventional missions in 2040, Bellanger told the National Assembly’s defense committee in a hearing here on Wednesday.
“We’re now moving on to work that will prefigure and enable the birth of this ACF, this future combat aircraft as a national program,” Bellanger said. France remains open to possible cooperation with other countries, “but within different frameworks and which won’t be structural to the birth of this aircraft.”
France and Germany agreed to scrap the FCAS project in June, after years of wrangling about specifications and industrial control between Dassault Aviation and Airbus. That’s left both countries without a clear successor for their existing fleets of Rafale and Eurofighter jets, respectively, though Germany has started receiving the first F-35 jets ordered in 2022 to replace the Panavia Tornado.
Dassault Aviation CEO Éric Trappier has said his company and France have all the know-how and skills to develop a next-generation fighter jet, together with engine partner Safran and defense-electronics firm Thales, and he would be able to do so “well below” a budget of €50 billion (US$56 billion).
All the years working on FCAS “haven’t been wasted,” with progress in areas including the aircraft, drones, stealth, connectivity and combat cloud, Bellanger said. Work had been split up in several so-called pillars that also included a new engine, with Dassault and Airbus working on the next-gen fighter pillar at the heart of the system.
“The halt of the FCAS program doesn’t mean we’re throwing everything away,” Bellanger said. “Our teams, the industrial teams have been working on the NGF, stealth, the cloud, and so on. All of that will allow us to continue at this stage on a national basis, while also focusing on this very important aspect of interoperability.”
France must “absolutely continue” working with Germany and other countries on the combat cloud, as interoperability between European crewed platforms will be vital, “to avoid thinking of a war fought side by side, but rather one fought together,” Bellanger said.
Bellanger said that even if FCAS wasn’t a success from an industrial standpoint, he has a very good working relationship with his German counterpart, with both commanders on the same page regarding their vision for future air combat, and both advocating for common operational requirements for the cloud component.
The Rafale successor will need to carry the ASN4G hypersonic nuclear cruise missile in 2050, and working back from that date means the aircraft will need to be flying in 2040 for conventional missions, Bellanger said. Moving ahead with a national program will allow France to meet the deadlines essential for nuclear deterrence by 2040, he said.
France will need to have a Rafale F5 standard in 2035 that incorporates the first components of the future combat aircraft, related to the engine, the sensors and the Stratus RS missile to neutralize enemy air defenses, according to Bellanger.
Bellanger said the British-Italian-Japanese GCAP project to develop a sixth-generation aircraft is working towards “a different kind of aircraft, it’s almost a strategic bomber.” He said “it’s not all roses” within the GCAP consortium, with cooperation inevitably requiring compromises.
The Air Force chief said France will receive its first long-range one-way munitions in the summer of 2027 with MBDA’s Deluge drone, which will form the basis for the country’s first squadron of bombing and reconnaissance drones. The force is also experimenting with interceptor drones with an eye on creating a dedicated drone-interceptor squadron.
The Air and Space Force further plans to create a very-high altitude squadron to deploy stratospheric balloons, which can be used for communication relays or as a platform for intelligence sensors, as well as other systems with long-endurance capabilities such as tethered balloons.
The air force envisages future strikes into enemy territory that will involve a first wave of a large number of disposable drones to weaken enemy air defenses, which will be the role of the new squadron, according to Bellanger. The disposable drones will be capable of kinetic operations, but also non-kinetic operations including jamming, saturation, or deception, the air force chief said.
A second wave of reusable but expendable drones would then create a breach to allow for deep strikes using crewed and uncrewed systems, he said.
“To strike the enemy on their own turf, we now have to think of overwhelming air defenses with low-cost bombing drones and electronic warfare capabilities such as offensive jamming.”
About Rudy Ruitenberg
Rudy Ruitenberg is a Europe correspondent for Defense News. He started his career at Bloomberg News and has experience reporting on technology, commodity markets and politics.

Leo Messi Has This Yacht on Order, It’s Not Meant Entirely for Him
6 photos
Photo: Sunreef
For one reason or another, yacht owners like to keep things private and are not very keen on being associated by name with the ships they own. From time to time, though, for unknown reasons, the identity of some yacht owners slips through the cracks, intentionally or not.
Take, for instance, an announcement made this week by Poland-based Sunreef Yachts , a name that becomes more and more common in the industry. The makers of sailing and power yachts from the 60, 70, 80, and 100 classes revealed in their statement the name of the newest high-profile individual to order a boat.
That would be the Inter Miami star Leo Messi, arguably the best and most well-known soccer player in history. Shortly after the man played the last game in the jersey of the Argentine national team, it became public knowledge that Messi ordered himself a brand-new yacht.
That would be the Sunreef Ultima 88 catamaran that’s presently under construction at the Sunreef facility in the UAE. The ship, it seems, is not meant to be used exclusively by Messi, as it has been commissioned for the soccer player’s MIM Ocean fleet. Based in the Balearic Islands, MIM is a luxury yacht charter company born from a collab between the soccer player and Med Cat Yachts.
The full details of this particular Sunreef 88 have not been made public yet, but there is talk of it featuring four guest cabins, a full beam master suite, an ocean lounge that allows access to swimming, water sports, and lounging, and even a dedicated jet ski garage.
Just like all the other 88s in the Sunreef portfolio, this one, too, will be powered by a pair of Volvo D13 engines capable of developing 1,000 horsepower each. That means the 88 can travel at top speeds of 20 knots (23 mph / 37 kph).
In standard configuration, the fiberglass-made multihull catamaran stands 88 feet (27 meters) long and features a 30.5 feet (9.31 meters) beam. There could be solar panels and other advanced energy solutions on deck to supply the ship’s energy needs.
We’ve seen another variant of the Sunreef 88 come to light earlier in September during the Cannes Yachting Festival. Called Wasabi , that one has been specced in such a way as to be able to accommodate ten people at a time and, true to its name, is equipped with a dedicated sushi chef's counter, designed not unlike the omakase tables you can see in certain Japanese restaurants.
As for the cost of such a yacht, it all depends on how much Messi’s desires stretch the yacht maker’s capabilities. It’s likely, though, that the starting price easily sits at around ten million dollars.
The Ultima 88 is part of a larger range of Sunreef yachts that also includes the 44, 55, 66, 77, 88, and the special edition 55 Brabus.

BYD used the Denza Z9 GT to showcase its latest breakthrough technology, including its 5-minute Flash Charging. Next year, the luxury GT will get another major update in Europe.
BYD confirms God’s Eye update for Denza in 2027
After unveiling the new Z9 GT in China earlier this year, BYD’s luxury sub-brand Denza claimed it was the “world’s longest pure electric driving range electric vehicle,” offering a CLTC range of up to 1,036 km (643 miles).
BYD launched the electric GT in Europe in July, its first vehicle in Europe to use its tri-motor e3 platform, second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging Technology.
The Denza Z9 GT kicked off “Europe’s Flash Charging revolution,” the company said, enabling drivers to charge up just as quickly as filling a gas tank.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Next year, BYD announced that Denza vehicles in Europe will receive an upgrade to its “God’s Eye” intelligent driving assistance system, adding “a new level” of urban driving ability.
Starting with the Z9 GT in 2027, Denza vehicles will receive City Navigation on Driving Assistant (CNOA) through an over-the-air (OTA) software update.
Denza Z9 GT interior (Source: Denza)
While average ADAS systems can handle straight-line driving on open roads, BYD said CNOA can manage point-to-point navigation in dense city driving.
The update will use the vehicle’s existing hardware, including a LiDAR, 12 ultrasonic radar sensors, three millimeter-wave radar sensors, and 11 cameras.
Once installed, the vehicle can automatically stop at red lights, yield at roundabouts, drive at the posted speed limit, make left turns, and change lanes around double-parked vehicles. It can also detect pedestrians, cyclists, and other objects in narrow city streets.
BYD Denza Z9 GT (Source: Denza)
Stella Li, BYD’s executive vice president, said that “We’re excited to fulfill our promise to bring the benefits of God’s Eye, including City Navigation on Driving Assistant, to the Z9GT.”
The hardware is already pre-installed, and the software is expected to be available in 2027 via an OTA update.
In Europe and the UK, the Denza Z9 GT is available in purely electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains.
BYD Denza Z9 GT (Source: Denza)
The all-electric version uses a 122.49 kWh battery pack and three electric motors, delivering a combined 1,140 hp (850 kW) and 892 lb-ft (1,210 Nm) of torque. Under WLTP conditions, the Denza Z9 GT offers up to 599 km (372 miles) of range.
With up to 1,500 kW of charging power, BYD’s Flash Charging stations offer what it calls “Ready in 5, Full in 9, Cold Add 3.”
In 5 minutes, the Denza Z9 GT can charge from 10% to 70%. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes just 9 minutes, and even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes only 3 minutes longer, replenishing the battery from 20% to 97% in 12 minutes.
The Denza GT is 5,195 mm long, 1,990 mm wide, and 1,480 mm tall, with a wheelbase of 3,125 mm, or about the size of the Porsche Panamera and Taycan.
In Europe, the Denza Z9 GT EV starts at €115,000 ($130,000), including VAT. In the UK, it’s priced from £105,000 ($139,000) for the EV variant. The plug-in hybrid (DM) starts at £95,000 ($126,000).

2026 Paris Motor Show • OMODA 4 Lands in Paris To Showcase Futuristic Styling, Looks Like a Discount Urus
Tesla Roadster Event Could Quite Literally Turn Explosive, Warns Elon Musk
11 photos
Photo: Tesla
In just a few hours, Tesla will show the twice-redesigned Roadster successor during an explosive event livestreamed all over the world. We can only speculate what the promised "epic demo" will show, but Elon Musk promised that it would be "a banger." Probably metaphorically, though Musk warned that the event might literally end with a bang.
Everyone is eagerly waiting for the clocks to show 7:55 PM CST at the SpaceX test facility in Waco, Texas, the time when the Roadster demo event is scheduled. The area is subject to flight restrictions until the end of October up to a 5,000-ft altitude. This suggests that no rocket is set to fly from the base. The restrictions are likely meant to prevent drone operators from flying over the facility.
Tesla has been unusually secretive about the Roadster, although some rumors have surfaced. The carmaker has offered a few hints over the past months, but the best we can do is speculate on them. The only things we know for sure are those that people expect to see at this event, and there's no guarantee that Tesla will oblige.
So, based on this, we will all be very disappointed if the redesigned Tesla Roadster won't fly during the demonstration. Elon Musk knows this as well, which is why I believe we will see such a demo tonight. The location of the event suggests that Tesla will use SpaceX technology to propel the Roadster into the air, even for a limited time.
Elon Musk appears to confirm this in a post on X about the Roadster event being "a candidate for greatest product demo of all time." He continued, saying that the demo "will be a BANGER, probably metaphorically, though some chance literally." This sounds like a warning that the demonstration could end up in flames, like one of his SpaceX rockets during so-called "Rapid Unscheduled Disassembly" (RUD) episodes.
The teasers Tesla has offered since September provide more hints of a flying Roadster, including the line "Where we're going..." written on the car's rear spoiler. The continuation is "we don't need roads," so go figure. The Roadster in the teaser invitation is also upside down, suggesting some sort of stunt prepared for tonight.
And that should be all about this evening: a PR stunt . There's nothing the second-generation Roadster could offer that hasn't been already tried. The Roadster's specifications could've been great in 2020 when it was supposed to start production, but in 2026 they're not. We've already had cars that accelerate 0-60 in under 2 seconds, and even some that can fly a little.
Other promises Tesla made in 2017 are pure fantasy even today, including the 620-mile range. Sure, it could be possible if the battery pack had 200 kWh of capacity, as Tesla promised in 2017, but this is still GMC Hummer territory today. Battery tech hasn't advanced that much, and energy density is still crap, which means a 200-kWh pack would still weigh over 2,500 lb. That would make the Roadster probably the worst sports car in history, at least as far as driving dynamics is concerned.
Even if the PR stunt succeeds in impressing the audience across the globe, that doesn't mean that Tesla will start production anytime soon, if ever. The Roadster doesn't make sense economically and technologically in today's world, especially as Musk has moved Tesla's goalposts beyond automotive. Earlier estimates for the Roadster's production start were 2027-2028, but that's difficult to imagine as possible, given the current development status. Let’s just say that this demo will be a BANGER, probably metaphorically, though some chance literally — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 15, 2026

Bugatti La Maison Pur Sang Redoes an Aluminum-Bodied Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse
13 photos
Photo: Bugatti
There are only three main models presently offered by Bugatti to its customers: the Tourbillon, W16 Mistral, and Bolide, and for most people who can afford any of these, that’s more than enough. There are some, however, that look for older models, especially the ones that are unique in one form or another. And this is where La Maison Pur Sang comes in.
The name hides, quite skillfully, Bugatti's official in-house heritage, restoration, and certification program, meaning the people tasked with digging up past Bugattis and bringing them back into the spotlight. And their most recent stunt is worthy of its 15 minutes of fame, again.
A little more than a decade ago, an unnamed customer with a passion for highly individualized cars asked Bugatti for a special version of the Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse, or something that’s nothing short of a work of art: an all-aluminum-bodied hypercar meant to shame other hypercars in all respects
Bugatti delivered, of course, and made the car’s almost entire bodywork from exposed polished aluminum. It needed quite a lot of metal of this kind: the carmaker says its people required massive blocks of aluminum that at times weighed up to 20 tons.
Left raw, the shiny stuff makes up the side panels in their entirety, with only small patches of exposed carbon fiber that can be seen here and there. At the same time, the interior leather has been specified in Carmine Red to deliver one of the most impactful contrasts known to man.
The roadster is known internally as chassis 8.100 and is animated by Bugatti’s 8.0-liter quad-turbocharged W16 engine that delivers 1,184 hp and 1,500 Nm of torque. What a sight this thing might be when going down the road...
The aluminum-bodied Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse is back in the spotlight after La Maison Pur Sang announced it has completed the refurbishment, reconfiguration, and certification process for the one-off, before sending it to its new owner on the French Riviera.
We’re told work on what is described as one of the most ambitious projects of the Veyron era was conducted using the documentation created back when the car was originally put together.
The focus of the team that did the work was to restore it to its original self, but Bugatti does not say what happened to it since it first rolled off the assembly lines to require such a thing. The only thing we’re informed on is that the process required the removal of later personalization elements, but no specifics are provided.
We also don’t know how much the thing cost to put back together, but word in the industry is that it originally cost more than double the price of a stock Veyron, which was around $2.5 million.

source_document.body:
Merck plans to invest $2.9 billion to expand vaccine and medicine manufacturing and drug research in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, by the end of 2030. State officials announced the news on Wednesday as the company opened a new research facility at its West Point site.
What’s Related
The $2.9 billion investment includes $550 million for the new ADVANCE facility at West Point and research facilities at nearby Spring House Innovation Park. Pennsylvania has also proposed a $5 million grant for the first West Point projects through its Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program.
Gov. Josh Shapiro and state economic development officials joined Merck leaders for the ADVANCE ribbon-cutting. The opening adds an automated laboratory to a site that already manufactures more than 200 million vaccine doses each year, according to the state.
“Merck’s major investment in Montgomery County is another major win for the Commonwealth,” said Shapiro.
RELATED STORIES: Merck to Build $3 Billion Manufacturing Facility in Virginia | Lilly Announces Plans For $3.5B Manufacturing Plant in Pennsylvania
Robots and AI for clinical research
The 120,000-square-foot ADVANCE facility uses robotics , automation, and AI to help analyze biological samples from Merck’s clinical development programs. That work helps researchers evaluate medicines and vaccines being tested in clinical trials.
“The ADVANCE facility represents the future of clinical development at Merck,” said Rob Davis, Merck’s chairman and CEO.
Merck says the laboratory will automate data handling and analysis to deliver results faster. It also expects automation to reduce human error and free scientists from routine tasks so they can spend more time on other research.
The company says its systems are designed to work together and adapt as laboratory technology changes. The laboratory will also use information management systems to organize samples, testing and research data.
A major vaccine manufacturing site
West Point covers 400 acres and is Merck’s largest combined research and human health manufacturing site. In addition to making and testing pharmaceuticals , vaccines, and biological products, it serves as a distribution center for other U.S. production sites.
Pennsylvania economic development Secretary Rick Siger said the state funding would help projects that “advance the development and manufacturing of critical medicines and vaccines.”
Merck acquired West Point through its 1953 merger with Sharp & Dohme. The company says it has invested more than $15 billion in the site over the past 35 years.
That construction spending has sustained an on-site workforce of about 800 people in contracting, engineering and construction jobs over that period, Merck said. The company also says many projects were designed in Pennsylvania, generating more than $1 billion in services for local architects.
The $550 million research investment at ADVANCE and Spring House is part of Merck’s previously announced $70 billion commitment to U.S. manufacturing and research.

source_document.body:
Maine Pointe and dSilo are expanding their partnership to connect purchasing and supplier data with customer pricing and demand. The agreement builds on more than five years of work between the supply chain consulting firm and the AI company.
What’s Related
Maine Pointe plans to incorporate dSilo’s AI agents into the next version of the Buy sourcing module within its TVO Control Tower software . The companies say the integration will help teams identify potential improvements, decide which to pursue first, and track the work.
The expanded partnership aims to help companies understand how supplier costs and customer agreements affect profit margins and cash available for daily operations. It links purchasing decisions with sales data .
According to the announcement, an earlier joint project processed more than 350,000 supplier invoices to examine pricing and purchasing volumes for individual items. The expansion will add AI agents intended to help teams act on those findings.
Checking what companies actually pay
The purchasing work addresses a practical question: Do invoices match the prices and terms a company negotiated? On its procurement product page, dSilo says its agents compare contracted prices with actual payments and flag differences.
The software can also compare prices for the same item from different vendors and examine changes by location and time. Those comparisons are intended to give buyers more information for supplier negotiations and purchasing decisions.
Other checks cover missed rebates, discounts and volume commitments. The company says its agents can compare contractual payment terms with actual payment dates, helping finance and purchasing teams investigate differences that affect cash.
The approach brings contract details together with transaction records. Teams can then check whether negotiated terms carried through to purchases and payments.
Moving from findings to action
On dSilo’s larger agent platform, a new invoice, contract amendment or price change can trigger a series of tasks. Specialized AI agents extract information, match records, and check results.
The company says businesses can require human review and approval at defined points, including contractual and financial decisions. Reviewers receive the supporting evidence alongside the recommendation, and approved actions can be sent back to existing business systems.
That platform supplies the technology behind the planned Maine Pointe integration. The companies intend to use it to help purchasing teams move from identifying pricing and contract issues to deciding what to address and tracking the resulting work.

1954 Ford C-600 COE Truck Is a Junkyard Survivor With a Rare John Deere Box
13 photos
Photo: Nobody's Show/YouTube
Now a widely used design, the cab-over-engine truck goes back to the early years of the automobile. The first modern COE hauler was introduced by White Motor Company in 1932, and the layout was adopted by most manufacturers over the next years.
In 1938, Ford became the first major manufacturer to offer a heavy-duty COE truck. The design improved maneuverability in the city and tight warehouse yards. The late 1940s saw the arrival of the C-Series, which became Ford's first COE with a tilting cab.
The C-Series remained in production for over four decades, becoming America's most iconic COE truck. And even though it may not be as popular as the F-Series pickup on the classic vehicle market, certain C-series models are getting a lot more attention these days. This is particularly true for the "helmet-shaped" haulers from 1948 to 1956.
One such truck recently arrived at Nobody Else's Auto junkyard in Great Bend, Kansas, and it's a sight to behold. It's a 1954 C-600, and it has a rare John Deere box behind the cab. The latter appears to have been used as a manure spreader.
The truck hasn't been used in decades, but it's still in relatively good shape. It's heavily weathered and has some rust, but it's still in one piece and appears to be an unrestored survivor. I can't confirm that it wasn't repainted at some point, but it's likely pretty original beyond that.
The John Deere box itself is a very rare sight nowadays. These units were usually dismantled when the truck they were on were retired. And most of those that survived rotted away beyond salvation. The C-600 still has the original powerplant under the hood; it's a Y-block V8 unit.
Speaking of which, these haulers were marketed as "triple economy" trucks back in the day. Ford advertised the three feats as "new gas-saving power," "new driver-saving efficiency," and "new money-saving payload capacities." The engine lineup included no fewer than five new powerplants.
In addition to the inline-six options used in light and medium trucks, Ford offered four different iterations of the Y-block V8. They were called "Cargo King" units, and displacement ranged between 239 and 317 cubic inches (3.9 to 5.2 liters). The C-600 came standard with the 239-cubic-inch V8, which was rated at 130 horsepower.
A quick peek inside the cabin reveals that the truck was ordered with the factory heater and radio, both of which are quite rare on these trucks. And the original units are still in place.
But is this truck worth saving? Well, since old COE haulers aren't very valuable in restoration condition, a refresh doesn't make much sense financially. This C-600 is probably better off as a parts vehicle. But I'd hate to see it being dismantled, so hopefully someone will make it his labor of love.
Check it out in the video below, which also shows quite a few brochures from the era. If you're into Ford memorabilia, this footage is definitely for you.

source_document.body:
Tesla’s latest crash reports to federal regulators add two more “Robotaxi” crashes where a remote operator, not the car’s autonomous system, was driving when it hit something.
That brings it to five in the data now. And every remote takeover that has shown up in a Tesla crash report has ended in a collision.
What the two new filings say
Both crashes happened in August and landed in NHTSA’s September release of Standing General Order data. Tesla now has 36 unique “Robotaxi” incident reports on file, up from 22 when we last looked at this in July .
In Dallas (report 13781-16678), a Model Y was stopped on a residential street, wedged between a concrete mixer truck on the right and a parked SUV on the left. “The remote support operator remotely took control and while moving forward, the vehicle made contact with the SUV at approximately 0.40MPH,” Tesla wrote. No passengers were aboard.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
In Austin (report 13781-16679), a remote operator “was in control” of a Model Y going straight through an alley, with a utility pole on one side and a dumpster on the other. It hit the dumpster at about 1 mph. Again, no passengers.
Both are property-damage-only, both are at walking speed, and both carry Tesla’s structured code for Driver/Operator Type: “Remote (Commercial / Test).” That’s the same field Tesla first used on the Houston tree-stump crash in May. Three of the five are now formally coded as remote operation.
Five crashes, same script
The other two show up only because Tesla unredacted its crash narratives in May . In July 2025 in Austin, a safety monitor couldn’t get the car to proceed, a teleoperator took over, accelerated, turned left, and drove it up a curb into a metal fence at 8 mph. In January 2026, again in Austin, a teleoperator took over for navigation help and drove into a construction barricade at 9 mph.
Line them up and it’s one script. The autonomous system gets stuck or needs help, a human takes the car over remotely, and the human crashes it.
Here’s the problem. Tesla doesn’t disclose how often remote operators intervene, so there’s no way to calculate a rate. But five remote takeovers have surfaced in the crash data, and all five ended in contact. Five for five.
Waymo draws the line somewhere else
Tesla’s main robotaxi competitor handles this differently, and it said so on the record. In a February 2026 letter to Senator Ed Markey, Waymo wrote that it “has not used remote driving or ‘tele-operations’ where a human performs the Dynamic Driving Task.” Its remote staff give the Waymo Driver guidance it can accept or reject. They don’t steer.
Waymo has one narrow exception, and it describes almost exactly these Tesla scenarios: a trained agent can nudge a stuck vehicle forward at 2 mph at fixed steering angles to clear a lane. Waymo says that tool has never been used outside of training.
So both companies built a way to rescue a stuck car. Waymo capped its version at a crawl with fixed steering and, by its own account, has never deployed it on a public road.
Electrek’s Take
We flagged this pattern in July with the Houston crash, and the data has added two more since. The severity still isn’t the story. Tesla’s robotaxis are already limited to surface streets at lower speeds, and it looks like speed is even more limited when remote operators take over.
Nobody’s been hurt, and we’re talking about bumpers, a dumpster, and a tree stump at walking speed.
What it shows is how often these cars still need a person to bail them out, and how badly that goes when one does. Teleoperation is the quiet part of the autonomy stack that nobody wants to talk about. Driving a car over a cellular or satellite link means latency, a limited view, and no physical feel for the vehicle.
If you own an EV, or a robotaxi ends up in your driveway someday, powering it with home solar is one of the cheapest ways to cut your charging costs to almost nothing. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. And with lease and PPA options, you can do it with zero upfront cost and start saving immediately. If you want to find the best deal, check out EnergySage . It’s a free service with hundreds of pre-vetted installers competing for your business, so you save 20 to 30% compared to going it alone. No sales calls until you pick an installer. Rivian Debuts Autonomy Early Access Program, Looks Like Its Own Take On the Tesla FSD Beta
14 photos
Photo: Rivian
Rivian is following in Tesla's footsteps with an early access program to test future Autonomy+ features before they are released to the rest of the fleet. The Autonomy Early Access Program will open in December to all owners with an active Autonomy+ subscription who apply. Access is restricted to a limited group, currently only in California and Florida.
Rivian prepares to debut more advanced features for its Autonomy+ driver assist system, which is currently offered exclusively on Gen-2 R1 vehicles and on the R2. The most exciting among them is Point-to-Point, which should close the gap with Tesla FSD .
Point-to-Point builds on the Universal Hands-Free capability and integrates it directly into the route navigation. With Point-to-Point, the vehicle will follow the active turn-by-turn directions in the navigation regardless of the road type. This should take you safely from the driveway to your destination, under your supervision, of course.
Many have been skeptical of Rivian's ability to develop in-house autonomous driving capabilities. Still, the EV startup is confident it could start rolling out Point-to-Point by the end of the year. The moment is crucial, as the company has a reputation for sticking to announced timelines. Well, except replacing the broken tonneau covers on early R1T vehicles, maybe.
That's not to say that Point-to-Point will be ready for prime time by then. Much like its bigger brother Tesla, Rivian will first start a beta-testing program, similar to Tesla FSD Beta . This would allow the carmaker to test future autonomous driving features in real-world conditions before they are deemed safe for a wider rollout to the Rivian fleet.
That's the role of the "Autonomy Early Access Program," which will begin testing new Point-to-Point features in December. Regular Autonomy+ subscribers will get Point-to-Point at a later date, hopefully early next year. That would be an impressive feat for Rivian, which doesn't have its own data centers as Tesla does.
The Autonomy Early Access Program is currently open only to Rivian owners with an Autonomy+ subscription in California and Florida. This means Gen2 R1S and R1T owners, as well as R2 owners. The program will be expanded in 2027, but Canadian owners would not be eligible.
Rivian expects the Autonomy Early Access Program to enroll a very limited number of Rivian owners. They will be evaluated on a monthly basis based on their driving behavior, and Rivian warns that their membership can be revoked at any time.
Interested owners will have to express interest in enrolling in the program through their Rivian account, even if it's not yet available in their region. Thus, they will not need to reapply if the program expands. The carmaker will favor eligible owners with high Autonomy feature usage and a clean recent safety record.
The Autonomy Early Access Program is expected to kick off during Rivian's second Autonomy & AI Day, which is scheduled for December 9 in San Francisco. The event should also provide the first real-world demonstration of Rivian's autonomous driving capabilities .

Richard “Rich” Francis, CEO of the collapsed R&R Family of Companies, has disclosed nearly $12.7 million in personal assets in a court filing on Wednesday.
Francis’ assets include an $8.5 million Florida waterfront residence, while reporting approximately $7.5 million in liabilities in newly filed federal bankruptcy documents.
The bankruptcy documents also disclose that Francis is employed by Giant Logistics LLC in a commissioned sales position making over $37,000 a month in gross wages.
The disclosures offer the most detailed accounting yet of Francis’ personal finances following the January shutdown of the Pittsburgh-based trucking and logistics group, which left hundreds of employees without jobs and prompted lawsuits from lenders, carriers and other creditors .
Francis filed his schedules and Statement of Financial Affairs in U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida, nearly three weeks after seeking personal Chapter 11 protection on Sept. 22.
The 47-page filing lists $12,670,208.96 in assets and $7,461,606.75 in liabilities. However, the schedules also identify several disputed, contingent or unliquidated claims without assigned dollar amounts, meaning the reported liabilities do not necessarily reflect Francis’ total potential financial exposure.
The documents provide new details about his real estate, personal property, financial transactions and employment following R&R’s collapse. They do not, however, provide a complete accounting of the former company’s assets, debts or remaining obligations to workers and creditors.
R&R’s operations shut down in January, leaving hundreds of employees across the country without jobs and carriers and other freight-related businesses pursuing unpaid invoices. (Photo: R&R)
Florida mansion at center of lender dispute
The largest asset disclosed is Francis’ residence at 550 S. Barfield Drive in Marco Island, Florida, which he values at $8.5 million.
He also lists two Pennsylvania properties: a residence in Presto valued at $1.4 million and a Pittsburgh property valued at $200,000.
Together, the three properties account for $10.1 million of his reported assets.
The Marco Island residence is central to litigation brought by Huntington National Bank , one of R&R’s principal lenders.
In a lawsuit filed in Collier County, Florida, Huntington alleged that R&R Express Properties LLC transferred the residence to Francis and his wife, Kathleen, in December 2025, as the company’s financial condition deteriorated.
The bank has challenged the transfer, alleging that it was intended to place the property beyond the reach of creditors. Those allegations have not been established by a court.
Francis’ bankruptcy schedules list a $5.3 million secured claim associated with Huntington, but an accompanying filing disputes his personal liability for the mortgage.
According to the notes, the mortgage is in the name of R&R Express Properties rather than Francis individually. The notes also describe a potential claim against Huntington involving an attempted mortgage payoff, the return of funds and a transaction involving Centennial Bank.
Francis additionally claims a Florida homestead exemption of $3.2 million for the Marco Island residence and identifies another exemption basis involving the same property. The claims have not been established as valid by a bankruptcy court, and the listed amounts should not be treated as separate exemptions that can automatically be added together.
The notes caution that none of the scheduled property values is based on a formal appraisal and that Francis reserves the right to amend the figures.
A 99-year lease raises additional questions
Another unusual disclosure involves a long-term lease for the Marco Island residence.
The court filing identifies a 99-year lease between Francis and R&R Express Properties LLC, with monthly rent of $16,667.67 plus expenses.
In the accompanying notes, Francis states that the lease was entered into at or near the time R&R Express Properties originally acquired the residence.
The filings do not establish whether the lease payments were made consistently, whether the agreement remains in effect or how the lease relates to the December 2025 transfer challenged by Huntington.
Francis reports new $37K monthly income from Giant Logistics
The bankruptcy documents also disclose that Francis is employed by Giant Logistics LLC in a commissioned sales position.
Court filings report approximately $37,078 in monthly gross wages and commissions from the company. Francis indicates that he began the position roughly two months before filing his bankruptcy petition.
His reported combined household monthly income, including other sources, is $42,751.54.
However, his monthly expenses total $65,283.45, producing a reported monthly deficit of $22,531.91.
Francis anticipates that his commissions from Giant Logistics could increase substantially as the business grows, projecting an additional approximately $22,000 per month within six months and $40,000 per month within a year. He does not explain how the business could grow in the court filing.
The schedules do not establish whether Giant Logistics has ownership, management or financial ties to R&R Family of Companies or whether it acquired any of the former company’s customers, employees or assets.
Boats, vehicles and other assets disclosed
Beyond real estate, Francis lists several personal assets, including a 2023 Boston Whaler 420R Outrage boat valued at $900,000 and two Sea-Doo personal watercraft valued at $3,500 each.
His schedules also identify luxury watches, household furnishings, bank accounts and interests in trusts.
Court documents disclose several transactions during 2026, including a wine collection transferred to Benchmark Wine Group in March for a reported $163,000, a 1961 Corvette transferred that month in a transaction valued at $160,000, and six timeshare interests transferred in May for a reported $60,000.
The Corvette disclosure also references approximately $148,000 in associated debt.
Francis also identifies interests in the Richard S. and Kathleen L. Francis Revocable Trust and the Kathleen L. Francis Spousal Lifetime Access Trust, with certain values listed as unknown.
What the disclosures reveal about R&R’s collapse
R&R Family of Companies operated a network of trucking, freight brokerage and logistics businesses, including R&R Express, RFX and Taylor Express.
Its operations began shutting down in January amid mounting financial pressures and disputes over unpaid freight bills.
Huntington has alleged in separate litigation that the R&R businesses suffered substantial losses and accumulated tens of millions of dollars in unpaid trade obligations before operations ceased.
In a separate lawsuit filed Jan. 23 in Hidalgo County, Texas, Jimenez Logistics LLC accused R&R Express Inc. and RFX Inc. of failing to pay approximately $264,650 in freight invoices for transportation services arranged in 2025 and early 2026. The complaint alleges that the companies continued arranging shipments despite knowing, or having reason to know, they could not pay carriers.
Jimenez Logistics asserted claims including breach of contract, fraudulent inducement and negligent misrepresentation. The allegations have not been proven in court.
Those claims remain allegations, and Francis’ personal bankruptcy schedules do not independently establish the company’s final financial condition.
The newly filed documents do, however, show how the financial fallout has extended beyond R&R’s operating businesses to Francis’ personal assets, guarantees, real estate and relationships with lenders.
Huntington National Bank filed a federal lawsuit against R&R-related companies on June 8, alleging they owe more than $12 million under a shared lending arrangement. (File photo: Jim Allen/FreightWaves)
The schedules list multiple R&R-related entities among parties connected to Francis’ financial obligations, while identifying potential claims against Huntington.
The Statement of Financial Affairs document reports approximately $3.18 million in wages and commissions during 2024, providing additional context for Francis’ compensation before the company’s collapse.
Another unresolved question is whether R&R’s corporate entities will seek bankruptcy protection of their own. Francis’ Chapter 11 is an individual proceeding and does not automatically place R&R Express, RFX, Taylor Express or other affiliates into bankruptcy.
Without a corporate bankruptcy proceeding, employees and trade creditors may have to pursue separate wage claims, lawsuits or collection actions against the specific entities that owe them money.
The amount ultimately available to satisfy those claims remains unclear.
Creditors prepare for next stage
Francis’ bankruptcy case is drawing participation from parties involved in the wider R&R financial dispute.
Attorneys representing Michael P. Williams and several AGX Freight-related companies filed notices of appearance Oct. 14. AGX was another freight business affected by financial disputes involving R&R and Huntington.
The appearances indicate that those parties are participating in or monitoring the proceedings, but do not themselves establish the validity or amount of any claim.
The bankruptcy court has scheduled an initial status conference for Oct. 21 and a meeting of creditors for Oct. 27.
The creditors’ meeting could provide an opportunity for questions about Francis’ finances, the disputed Marco Island property, his current business activities and the relationship between his personal obligations and R&R’s collapse.
FreightWaves contacted Francis’ bankruptcy attorney, Michael Seese, by email and telephone but did not receive a response to requests for comment.
Why it matters: R&R Family of Companies CEO’s bankruptcy filings offer new insight into his assets, business activities and financial obligations, but leave unresolved whether creditors and former employees can recover money owed by the company.

Man Buys New Lucid Air Touring for $128,550 in 2023, Sells for $35,250 in 2026
21 photos
Photo: Cars & Bids/autoevolution
I wouldn't blame you for wondering what on Earth is happening to used Lucid Air models right now. If you bought one of these EVs brand-new a few years ago and are looking to sell, well, you're basically screwed. There's no nicer way to put it. These numbers are truly difficult to stomach.
Back in June, I wrote about a similar 2023 Lucid Air Touring, except that one cost nearly $100,000 new and then exchanged hands for just $42,000. I thought it was a great deal for the buyer, especially since the car only came with 18,500 miles on the clock. For the seller... it was painful, but within parameters.
This latest Air Touring sale makes that previous deal look downright conservative. Again, this is a 2023 model that cost its original owner $128,550. Fast forward to last week, when this was sold at auction for $35,250. That's right, a staggering $93,300 gone in roughly 3.5 years. That's nearly 73% of its original value. Yes, it's a high-mileage car with 49,300 miles (79,000 km) on the odometer, but still.
Losing 73% of the original value pretty much makes your car a shipwreck. Next thing you know people will just be giving these away, sort of like what's been happening with the Fisker Ocean. Let me frame it another, even more painful way. You could buy a brand-new and very well-specified 2027 BMW i5 M60 with the money this Lucid lost in depreciation since new. By the way, you can check out our review of the i5 M60 right here .
I know that luxury sedans have never been particularly good at retaining their value, but expensive battery-electric sedans are on a whole different level of vulnerability on the used car market. The fact that Lucid struggles with consumer confidence is yet another issue at play.
Now, as far as I'm concerned, the Air Touring is by no means a bad car. One might say this one in particular is quite the steal for the price of a run-of-the-mill family crossover.
Photo: Cars & Bids According to the ad , the car has already been serviced to within an inch of its life, and there are currently no significant known flaws. Here's a list of everything that's been replaced following maintenance: TPMS, wipers and coolant port valve, A-pillar and hood duct, cabin air filter and wipers, battery terminal, windshield, A/C compressor, active grille shutter, front door release, and the high-voltage battery.
In terms of specs, this comes in Cosmos Silver Metallic featuring 19" Aero Range wheels, a glass canopy roof, leather upholstery, power-adjustable and ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, a heated steering wheel, the Surreal Sound system, and more.
Power comes from a dual-motor setup working alongside a 92-kWh battery pack, sending 620 horsepower to all four wheels. All things being equal, that's a lot of performance for $35k. Just saying.

source_document.body:
Maine Pointe and dSilo are expanding their partnership to connect purchasing and supplier data with customer pricing and demand. Announced Oct. 13, the agreement builds on more than five years of work between the supply chain consulting firm and the AI company.
What’s Related
Maine Pointe plans to incorporate dSilo’s AI agents into the next version of the Buy sourcing module within its TVO Control Tower software . The companies say the integration will help teams identify potential improvements, decide which to pursue first, and track the work.
The expanded partnership aims to help companies understand how supplier costs and customer agreements affect profit margins and cash available for daily operations. It connects purchasing decisions with information from the sales side of a business .
According to the announcement, an earlier joint project processed more than 350,000 supplier invoices to examine pricing and purchasing volumes for individual items. The expansion will add AI agents intended to help teams act on those findings.
Checking what companies actually pay
The purchasing work addresses a practical question: Do invoices match the prices and terms a company negotiated? On its procurement product page, dSilo says its agents compare contracted prices with actual payments and flag differences.
The software can also compare prices for the same item from different vendors and examine changes by location and time. Those comparisons are intended to give buyers more information for supplier negotiations and purchasing decisions.
Other checks cover missed rebates, discounts, and volume commitments. The company says its agents can compare contractual payment terms with actual payment dates, helping finance and purchasing teams investigate differences that affect cash.
The approach brings contract details together with transaction records. Teams can then check whether negotiated terms carried through to purchases and payments.
Moving from findings to action
On dSilo’s broader agent platform, a new invoice, contract amendment, or price change can start a series of tasks. Specialized AI agents extract information, match records, and check results.
The company says businesses can require human review and approval at defined points, including contractual and financial decisions. Reviewers receive the supporting evidence alongside the recommendation, and approved actions can be sent back to existing business systems.
That platform supplies the technology behind the planned Maine Pointe integration. The companies intend to use it to help purchasing teams move from identifying pricing and contract issues to deciding what to address and tracking the resulting work.

The American Trucking Associations has turned to one of its affiliates and plucked the head of the Alabama Trucking Association to be the national group’s next president and CEO, effective December 1.
Mark Colson has been named to head the ATA, which was jolted by the sudden departure of Chris Spear in late August.
According to a statement released by ATA, Colson has been president and CEO of the Alabama Trucking Association since 2019. Prior to that, he worked for several Alabama-based business organizations, including the Business Council of Alabama.
Colson, according to ATA, has been active in the group’s activities. He has been a member of the association’s Strategic Priorities Committee and the Truck PAC Board of Directors. Colson also is on the Advisory Committee of the American Transportation Research Institute, the ATA’s research arm.
According to ATA, Colson was elected by his peers at other ATA state associations as vice chairman of the Trucking Association Executives Council.
He is the 10th ATA president and CEO in the group’s history, which dates back to 1933. He is a graduate of Huntingdon College, and receive an MBA from Troy University.
The chairman of the Alabama Trucking Association, Scott Smith who is CEO of PS Logistics, praised Colson’s tenure with that group. Colson, Smith said, “grew our membership and broke revenue records year over year for all our entities, and established our political action committee as one of the best and most effective in the state.”
In the ATA prepared statement, Colson said his role as head of Alabama Trucking “has been the honor of my career.”

First Sneak Peek at the Porsche Mission S Just Before You're Supposed To See It
7 photos
Photo: kingofthecrest | Instagram
Footage of Porsche’s highly anticipated Mission S supercar has leaked online just hours before its scheduled world premiere in New York. The video captured by onlookers during an official photo shoot shows it as those around it remove the tarp, exposing a radical new design that breaks away from anything you have seen from Porsche production cars over the years.
The concept car serves as the star of Porsche’s new Sportwagenschmiede 2035 , the plan that shifts the automaker's core philosophy from chasing sales volume to prioritizing high-margin, ultra-luxury exclusivity in order to restore brand profitability.
The leaked footage captured from a high point reveals the muscular rear end and the low-slung, mid-engined silhouette, inspired by classic Porsche racing heritage. The biggest surprise, which caused massive stir online, is the top-mounted cooling fan integrated into the rear decklid, which is a direct nod to the legendary Porsche 917 air-cooled race cars.
The Mission S features prominent rear fenders that envelop the tail, paired with an integrated hoop-style rear spoiler, which reminds Porsche enthusiasts of the iconic 959. The twin-turbocharged supercar manufactured by Porsche from 1986 to 1993 was originally developed as an ultra-high-tech Group B rally car, before it was adapted into a road-legal production model to meet racing requirements.
Photo: kingofthecrest | Instagram The roof features Bugatti Chiron-like split glass panels, leading down to an aggressive high-downforce setup, which integrates a massive rear diffuser and stacked quad exhausts. Porsche has been quite secretive about the powertrain of its Mission S , but no, it is not an EV.
All speculation points to an all-new, in-house developed 5.0-liter flat-eight engine. The bespoke boxer power plant is rumored to rev up to 8,000 rpm and is expected to be integrated into a plug-in hybrid setup, which means there will be at least one electric motor to assist it.
Rumors have it that the setup will push out between 700 and 750 horsepower (710 to 760 metric horsepower) for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 2.8 seconds and a top speed in excess of 200 mph (322 kph).
Right now, Porsche's quickest car is the Taycan Turbo S with 1,019 horsepower (1,034 metric horsepower) and a 0 to 60 time in a neck-snapping 1.9 seconds. The production version of the Porsche Mission S will serve as the spiritual successor to the Carrera GT and the 918 Spyder.
Photo: kingofthecrest | Instagram The cabin of the Mission S has also been a top secret at Porsche these past few months, but the car is expected to get a classic, Carrera GT-inspired instrument cluster and at least three distinct driving modes: Normal, Sport, and Track.
The Porsche Mission S will make its official debut later today, at 4:30 PM Eastern Time, in New York. That is when we will get all the official numbers. View this post on Instagram A post shared by "Porsche Content By General Manager Al H” (@kingofthecrest)
